title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are buzzing with activity, from funding rounds to strategic partnerships. As nations sign onto the Artemis Accords and the Space Force expands its capabilities, the landscape is shifting, albeit with the usual bureaucratic hiccups.

themes.title: Funding Frenzy in Space Tech
themes.body: AI-driven startups are attracting significant investments, with LegendSpace's $29.5 million angel round highlighting the trend. Meanwhile, True Anomaly's $190 million Series C underscores the growing appetite for space domain awareness technologies.

themes.title: International Cooperation Gains Momentum
themes.body: Mauritius joining the Artemis Accords marks the 70th nation to sign on, reflecting a broader commitment to collaborative lunar exploration. This is a significant step towards a more unified approach in space governance.

themes.title: Military Space Initiatives Expand
themes.body: The Space Force's tripling of launch contract ceilings indicates a robust demand for military space capabilities. Furthermore, the Pentagon's $7.1 million investment in satellite cover glass production signals a push for domestic manufacturing in critical areas.

themes.title: Tech Partnerships on the Rise
themes.body: Anduril and L3Harris teaming up for a tactical satellite constellation bid illustrates the trend of defense firms consolidating resources for competitive advantage. This collaboration could enhance capabilities in an increasingly crowded space.
